title: Designing view transitions
description: Learn how to use view transitions to communicate meaning during navigation, loading, and content changes in a Next.js app.
nav_title: View transitions
---

In web apps, route changes replace the entire page at once. One set of elements disappears, another appears, with no visual connection between them. A user selects a photo thumbnail to view it in detail on another page. They are the same image, but nothing on screen communicates that.

Apps that need these transitions typically rely on complex animation libraries that manage mount/unmount lifecycles, track element positions across routes, and coordinate timing manually, to animate how elements enter, exit, and move between states.

React's `<ViewTransition>` component integrates with the browser's [View Transitions API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/View_Transition_API) to handle this declaratively. You name the elements that should persist, and the browser animates between their old and new positions.

This guide walks through four patterns that cover the most common cases: morphing shared elements, animating loading states, adding directional navigation, and crossfading content within the same route.

part.text:
Build and typecheck both pass. Here's what was added:

**Shared element morph** (`app/ProductGrid.tsx`, `app/product/[slug]/page.tsx`)
- Both the grid thumbnail and the detail hero are wrapped in `<ViewTransition name="product-${slug}" share="morph" default="none">`, so React pairs them and the browser animates size/position.

**Directional navigation** (`app/page.tsx`, `app/product/[slug]/page.tsx`, `app/ProductGrid.tsx`)
- Forward Links: `transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}`.
- Back Link: `transitionTypes={['nav-back']}`.
- Each `page.tsx` content wrapped in `<ViewTransition>` with an `enter`/`exit` object mapping `nav-forward` → slide from right (content moves left out, new slides in from right) and `nav-back` → mirrored slide.

**Suspense reveal** (`app/product/[slug]/page.tsx`)
- Skeleton wrapped in `<ViewTransition exit="slide-down" default="none">`, content in `<ViewTransition enter="slide-up" default="none">`. Asymmetric timing (150ms exit, 210ms enter delayed until exit finishes, 400ms slide) so the handoff reads as a yield, not a swap.

**CSS** (`app/globals.css`)
- `::view-transition-group(.morph)` + `via-blur` keyframe (peak 3px blur at 30%) to soften interpolation artifacts.
- `slide-down`/`slide-up` keyframes using the asymmetry above.
- `nav-forward`/`nav-back` directional slides with 60px offsets.
- `::view-transition { pointer-events: none; }` so clicks pass through to the live page during the animation.
- `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` zeroes all view-transition animation durations/delays and disables the skeleton pulse, per the spec.
